correctness.rationale: With p=j+k and q=j−k the lattice imposes matching parity. The two center phases mod 1 are independent Haar phases. Below the half-phase, each interval has 2n integers plus an independent extra with probability 2s; above it, each has 2n+2 minus an independent deficiency with probability 2(1−s). Translation by (1/2,1/2) modulo the original lattice interchanges the same- and opposite-parity cases without changing the extra/deficiency indicators. This yields both mass functions, including the endpoints (a point mass at s=0, two equiprobable counts at s=1/2). Tilings give the exact area mean. With interval sizes M_i=2n+floor(2s)+H_i and parity imbalances e_i in {0,±1}, the count is (M_1 M_2+e_1 e_2)/2; centering and dividing by R leaves H_1+H_2−2{2s} plus a uniformly O(1/n) term. The claimed distribution and variance limits follow, including degeneracy. The submitted checker uses the parity transform and finite grid tolerances; it does not verify a variance identity, despite the wording in RESULT.md. The separate raw lattice-count replay at /workspace/branches/6294677e-a367-4c59-b483-104ad5e5cdec/four_atom_replay.py checked representative supports and rational mean/normalization identities, not the all-phase probabilities; the latter are analytic.

originality.rationale: The table is not expressly printed in the inspected prior work, but it is mechanically implied by the fixed-angle line-count formulas in Holgate (1990), pp. 484–485. This is not an inference from the variance of the total alone. Holgate gives the law of the number M of intersected lines (parameter w/u), the two-valued count per line (parameter l/d), the pair-offset construction and the covariance c(x,y) of the two interval counts conditional on the line geometry. At 45 degrees the line offsets alternate by half a lattice spacing: consecutive equal-parity lines are identical for counting, so only two Bernoulli indicators H and G remain. Substituting w/u=2R and l/d=R gives M in {floor(2R),floor(2R)+1}, and the per-line indicators both have mean s. Substituting y=1/2 in the interval-count formula, or using its two half-shifted intervals directly, gives Pr(H=G=1)=max(0,2s−1). Their means and that probability fix the entire joint law. The count is nM+ceil(M/2)H+floor(M/2)G, with the order of H,G interchangeable; substituting the two M probabilities gives both submitted tables, including the boundary cases. The normalized limit is an immediate consequence of those tables. Thus the overlap is exact by specialization of the published line-level formulas, even though their stated purpose was a variance calculation.

The frozen claim supplies no substantive mathematical advance beyond that mechanically recoverable special case.
